revision_history.description: Added the fault_reaction this requirement was missing, derived from the source rather than from the synthetic concept. This is an as_is record with origin source_observed, so a reaction copied from the synthetic_reference copy would have been a claim about the real implementation that the implementation does not support. What the source does is graded by DIAG severity and the record now says so: DIAG_ID_AFE_CELL_VOLTAGE_MEAS_ERROR is configured DIAG_WARNING with DIAG_DELAY_DISCARD (src/app/engine/config/diag_cfg.c:180) and does NOT open the contactors, whereas DIAG_ID_AFE_SPI, DIAG_ID_AFE_COMMUNICATION_INTEGRITY, DIAG_ID_AFE_MUX and DIAG_ID_AFE_CONFIG are DIAG_FATAL_ERROR with DIAG_SEN_EVENT_5 and DIAG_DELAY_100ms (diag_cfg.c:159-162), and a fatal entry is one the configuration's own comment says will lead to an opening of the contactors (diag_cfg.h:287). The aggregation path - BMS_IsAnyFatalErrorFlagSet() at src/app/application/bms/bms.c:515-531 taking the shortest active delay, BMS_IsBatterySystemStateOkay() at bms.c:534-575, and the transition to BMS_FSM_STATE_OPEN_CONTACTORS at bms.c:1197-1204 - is recorded because it is the mechanism and not the outcome that makes the reaction auditable. As with the synthetic copy, element_owns_reaction is false and the reason is stated: AR-001 is allocated detection, not a reaction, in both concepts. open_limits records that the DIAG sensitivity is a COUNT of handler calls (src/app/engine/diag/diag.c:287-301) rather than a time window, so its wall-clock value depends on the BMS task period and not on anything this requirement states, and that no measurement of any of these intervals exists. Statement, rationale, all five acceptance criteria, safety_allocation, the ASIL and the safety goal reference are unchanged and no threshold was relaxed. Human approval remains pending, production_authorized stays false and product_verification_credit stays false. This is a statement about what the code at the pinned commit does; it is not evidence that the requirement is met, and no ASIL, certification or capability level is claimed for the real product.

statement: The BMS shall acquire all cell voltages from AFE slaves at a minimum rate of 20 Hz with PEC/CRC validation, and publish validated data to the database within 25 ms of acquisition trigger.
rationale: Required for SOA monitoring to detect overvoltage/undervoltage within FTTI

acceptance_criteria.measure: Time from SPI complete to database write

fault_reaction.reaction: No reaction is allocated to AR-001, and the reason is structural rather than an omission: FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 places fault_detection on AR-001 and allocates its four reactions to AR-002, AR-004, AR-005 and AR-006, and FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 says the same thing in its strategy_allocation. What the real implementation does when this chain fails is stated here so the requirement is not read as reactionless, and it splits by DIAG severity rather than uniformly. A measurement that fails its own validity check is reported as DIAG_ID_AFE_CELL_VOLTAGE_MEAS_ERROR, which src/app/engine/config/diag_cfg.c:180 configures at severity DIAG_WARNING with sensitivity DIAG_SEN_EVENT_1 and delay DIAG_DELAY_DISCARD, so it does NOT open the contactors by itself. A link failure is different: DIAG_ID_AFE_SPI, DIAG_ID_AFE_COMMUNICATION_INTEGRITY, DIAG_ID_AFE_MUX and DIAG_ID_AFE_CONFIG are all configured at severity DIAG_FATAL_ERROR with sensitivity DIAG_SEN_EVENT_5 and DIAG_DELAY_100ms (diag_cfg.c:159-162), and a DIAG_FATAL_ERROR entry is one whose comment at src/app/engine/config/diag_cfg.h:287 states will lead to an opening of the contactors. The reaction that follows is the one described for FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 and FB2-SAF-FSR-000003: the fatal flag is aggregated by BMS_IsAnyFatalErrorFlagSet() in src/app/application/bms/bms.c:515-531, the shortest active delay is taken as minimumActiveDelay_ms, BMS_IsBatterySystemStateOkay() at bms.c:534-575 returns STD_NOT_OK once that delay has elapsed, and the state machine is driven into BMS_FSM_STATE_OPEN_CONTACTORS with nextState BMS_FSM_STATE_ERROR (bms.c:1197-1204).
fault_reaction.triggered_by: A cell-voltage word the AFE driver reports as invalid via DIAG_CheckEvent(cellVoltageMeasurementValid, DIAG_ID_AFE_CELL_VOLTAGE_MEAS_ERROR, ...) at src/app/driver/afe/ltc/ltc_6806.c:457 (severity WARNING - no contactor opening), or an SPI / communication-integrity failure reported as DIAG_ID_AFE_SPI or DIAG_ID_AFE_COMMUNICATION_INTEGRITY at ltc_6806.c:699-961 (severity FATAL - contactors open after the configured delay).

reaction_held_by.reaction: Aggregate the fatal diagnosis flags and, after the configured delay, drive the state machine into BMS_FSM_STATE_OPEN_CONTACTORS
reaction_held_by.reaction_time_budget_basis: DIAG_DELAY_100ms from diag_cfg.c:159-162. This is the delay between the flag becoming active and the state request, not the whole reaction; BMS_IsAnyFatalErrorFlagSet() takes the SHORTEST delay among all active fatal entries (bms.c:522-527), so a co-active overvoltage with its 200 ms delay would be overtaken by this one.

reaction_held_by.reaction: Execute the opening sequence and confirm by auxiliary feedback
reaction_held_by.reaction_time_budget_basis: Not a configured constant. The 40 ms is the synthetic_reference figure FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 allocates and is recorded on FB2-SAF-FSR-000003; the real implementation waits BMS_WAIT_TIME_AFTER_OPENING_STRING_CONTACTOR (10 ms, src/app/application/config/bms_cfg.h:128) after each contactor and drives the sequence from a 10 ms task period, so the real end-to-end time is governed by bms_cfg.h and by the mechanical contactor, not by this figure.

fault_reaction.mode_dependence: Mode-independent on the detection side: the integrity check and the SPI/communication diagnosis run the same way in every mode. The reaction is mode-dependent in the sense FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 records for AR-004: entering the safe state in MOD-004 removes propulsion from a moving vehicle.
fault_reaction.allocation_basis: FB2-SAF-FSC-000001.safety_strategies.fault_reaction allocates no reaction to AR-001; FB2-SAF-TSC-000001.safety_strategies.strategy_allocation states 'AR-001 and AR-005 detect, AR-002 confirms, AR-004 acts and confirms the action'. The severities and delays quoted above are read from src/app/engine/config/diag_cfg.c at the pinned commit recorded in docs/artifacts/sources/source-registry.json, and the aggregation and state transition are read from src/app/application/bms/bms.c.
fault_reaction.open_limits: Four limits are recorded and none is closed by this field. First, the DIAG severity split is not uniform across the failure modes of this chain and is not a property of this requirement: DIAG_ID_AFE_CELL_VOLTAGE_MEAS_ERROR is only a WARNING, so a measurement the driver knows to be invalid does not by itself reach the safe state, and what does reach it is the link failure that usually accompanies it. Nothing in this corpus analyses that pairing. Second, the sensitivity of a DIAG_SEN_EVENT_5 entry is a COUNT of DIAG_Handler calls, not a time window (DIAG_GetDiagnosisEntryState at src/app/engine/diag/diag.c:287-301 compares an occurrence counter against the configured threshold), so the wall-clock time of the debounce depends on how often SOA and the AFE drivers are called, which is the BMS task period BMS_STATEMACHINE_TASK_CYCLE_CONTEXT_MS = 10 (src/app/application/config/bms_cfg.h:100) and not anything this requirement states. Third, no measurement of any of these intervals exists. Fourth, AR-005's independence is assumed (FB2-ASM-008) and not demonstrated, so the last-resort reaction in reaction_held_by is an intention.

safety_allocation.mitigation: PEC/CRC, database integrity, independent HW monitor, plausibility
